content: Anthranilic acid is an organic compound with the chemical formula C6H4(NH2)CO2H. In its pure form, it appears as a white solid, although commercially available samples may have a yellowish tint. The structure of anthranilic acid consists of a benzene ring with two adjacent functional groups: a carboxylic acid (-CO2H) and an amine (-NH2). Due to the polar nature of these functional groups, anthranilic acid exhibits high solubility in water. It is occasionally referred to as vitamin L. In biological systems, anthranilic acid is synthesized from chorismic acid. It serves as a precursor to the amino acid tryptophan, a process that involves the attachment of a ribose molecule to the amine group of anthranilic acid. Anthranilic acid has a variety of industrial and commercial applications. It is used as an intermediate in the production of dyes, pigments, and the artificial sweetener saccharin. Additionally, anthranilic acid and its esters are utilized in the formulation of perfumes, pharmaceuticals, and ultraviolet (UV) light absorbers. It also functions as a corrosion inhibitor for metals and as a mold inhibitor in soy sauce. In organic synthesis, anthranilic acid can be employed to generate the benzyne intermediate, which is a reactive species used in various chemical reactions.
